messages.author: 7cb6d72715db48b6
messages.subject: running SSE_simtrait simulation
parts:
Dear colleagues,
I am trying to validate my model, after running a model comparison routine with BiSSE models, with the routine "run_SSE_simtrait_v2.R"
I have gotten the following error:
Error in modify_Qmat_with_trait(Qmat = NULL, BioGeoBEARS_run_object = BioGeoBEARS_run_object,  :
  argument "numstates_geogtrait" is missing, with no default


Besides when I put my own traits, I have also an error. It seems that the tip labels are not matching. I have noticed that the routine of Kristina Klaus (Podocarpaceae) has no tree, but it seems that it could be possible. Have anyone tried to run that routine?
My best regards,
José Ricardo.

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: running SSE_simtrait simulation
parts:
Hi!  Apologies for missing this earlier -- some other part of the code probably changed since the analysis was run for the Klaus & Matzke paper.  I added a line to the modify_Qmat_with_trait() function, and posted it to GitHub, this seems to fix the issue.

I suggest:

1. Reinstall from GitHub: https://github.com/nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github(repo="nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS")

2. Restart R

3. Run the attached script (simplified from the Supp. Mat version), making sure to 
(a) set the location of master_wd somewhere sensible on your machine
(b) create a "sims" directory inside of that directory

...and it should work!  This is a 4-area, 2-trait simulation, followed by inference under a variety of models.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: running SSE_simtrait simulation
parts:
Hi -- I think the number of ranges is set automatically when you load your ranges file.  The practical size limit is that the number of states should be <1500 or so, where the number of states is something like 2^(number_of_areas + number_of_trait_states).

Cheers,
Nick

On Thu, Sep 15, 2022 at 2:29 AM José Ribeiro <jozeca...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, Nick. Thank you.  I am trying to simulate using a distance matrix with different periods of time (because my best model was a time-stratified one). Given that I added a file with distance matrices through different slices of time, do the simulations take this into account? I mean do the simulations run under different transition probability matrices over epochs?
My best regards,
José Ricardo.

Hi -- the biogeographic stochastic maps will take into account changing distances, changing dispersal-multiplier matrices, etc., yes.  

The simulations from scratch, where the tree is simulated as well -- I'm pretty sure this would *not* work.  Among other challenges, when you simulate the whole tree, you don't know how old the tree will be when the simulation stops.  Times in time-stratification are applied from the present, backwards in time, so it would be quite challenging to design a simulator that would produce trees that would be just the right age.  Probably the approach would be brute-force, i.e. do hundreds of simulations under changing geography, and select the few that end up about the right age.  But, it would be a fairly major project to code that.

Cheers,
Nick

On Sunday, September 4, 2022 at 7:28:16 PM UTC-3 nickmat...@gmail.com wrote:
